study type: Mixed-methods (cross-sectional survey and focus group discussions)
exposure: Standards of structure and process of antenatal service
Definition of male partners' role in maternal health care system
cohort: The study included 428 nursing mothers and 18 male partners of women attending antenatal clinics and nursing mothers in the post-natal ward.
finding: The prevalence of male partners' involvement in antenatal care was 69%, and this involvement depended on access to antenatal care education, standards of antenatal service, and the definition of their role within the maternal health care system.
cross-section timing: Data was collected from nursing mothers and partners of women in the post-natal ward (postpartum), and partners of women attending antenatal clinics (antenatal period).
